item.description: This week is Catholic Schools Week. The Mass was celebrated by Bishop Kevin Doran in St Joseph's Church. item.title: Gardaí continue to probe suspected petrol bomb attack in Athlone
item.description: An investigation is continuing into a suspected petrol bomb attack in Athlone. The incident happened in the Magazine Avenue area of Battery Heights area of the town in the early hours of last Thursday morning, January 15th. The local fire service extinguished the blaze and no injuries have been reported. Advertisement No arrests have been made and gardaí are appealing for information relating to the incident. item.title: Staff appointed to run new post office in Boyle
item.description: Four staff have been appointed to run the new post office in Boyle from next month. The business is currently located in a historic building in Shop Street, which will close at the end of January. From February 3rd, it will be located in a former cafe and restaurant beside Kelly's Supervalu. Advertisement The supermarket's owner, Paul-Henry Kelly, says excellent staff will run it, as he told Eoghan Murphy.

item.title: The Walk in Roscommon town must be gritted urgently, council told
item.description: Roscommon County Council are facing calls to add a troublesome route to the local authority's gritting list. The L1807, known locally as The Walk, located in Roscommon town is home to a number of houses, while several companies operate in the locality and it is often used by parents with children in a nearby national school. Independent councillor Michael Holland feels a solution needs to be found, before it's too late: Advertisement

item.title: No one injured after truck crashes in Roscommon
item.description: No injuries have been reported after a crash in Co Roscommon. The single-vehicle collision, involving a truck, occurred in Ballinagare shortly after 10pm last night. Gardaí and emergency services attended the scene and there was traffic disruption for a time. Advertisement

item.title: 55 admitted patients stranded on trolleys in Sligo hospital
item.description: There were over 70 admitted patients waiting for a bed at local hospitals this morning. That's according to the INMO's latest trolley watch report. Wednesday's figures show there 55 patients waiting in Sligo University Hospital. Advertisement This included 26 in the emergency department and 29 on wards elsewhere. item.title: Farming Rathcroghan Project to cease operations
item.description: A pioneering and award-winning initiative in county Roscommon that has supported farmers in protecting one of Ireland’s most significant achaelogical landscapes, is set to cease operations on March 31st due to a lack of long-term funding. The announcement follows a recent meeting of Farming Rathcroghan Project’s Board of Management, at which all potential funding operations were considered. item.title: Government's Mercusor u-turn under fire
item.description: The government's approach to the Mercusor agreement has come under fire on the floor of the Dáil. It was decided late in the day to vote against the deal after it emerged Italy would support the deal. Earlier today, the majority of MEPs voted for it be referred to the European Court of Justice in the European Parliament. item.title: Dáil hears of impact of Longford health vacancy
item.description: The Dáil has heard a vital health job in Longford has been vacant for a year - badly impacting kids. Fine Gael TD Micheál Carrigy says there's a significant number of children on the waiting list for occupational therapy in the county. He says this is causing major problems for families. Advertisement The Longford-Westmeath TD raised the issue with Health Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill today: Minister Carroll MacNeill says she'll try to solve the issue: Advertisement

item.title: Local MEP recounts recent health scare
item.description: A Midlands North West MEP has detailed a recent medical procedure which saw him miss a vote on the EU-Mercusor deal. Luke 'Ming' Flanagan previously spoke out in opposition to the deal. However, he was unable to attend today's vote in Strasbourg due to a cyst on his jaw. Advertisement The Independent representative says he heeded medical advice: MEP Flanagan was also asked whether or not there was a timeline for his return: Advertisement
